c1-26-01.title: Communicative Challenge: How Sure Is the News
c1-26-01.scenario: You read a news item whose source has not confirmed it. Károly asks whether it is true.
c1-26-01.prompt: Tell Károly how sure you are.
cues: Say what you think of the news
Say that you cannot be sure
c1-26-01.target: A hír feltehetőleg hamis, de nem zárható ki, hogy van benne igazság.
c1-26-01.english: The news is probably false, but it cannot be ruled out that there is some truth in it.
c1-26-01.canDo: I can say how sure a news report is with *kétséget kizáróan*, *igazolhatóan*, *feltehetőleg* and *nem zárható ki, hogy*.

c1-26-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Misleading Article
c1-26-02.scenario: You have read an article with a quotation torn out of its context. Károly asks what is wrong with it.
c1-26-02.prompt: Tell Károly what is wrong with the article.
cues: Say what it does to the reader
c1-26-02.target: A kontextusból kiragadott idézet félrevezeti az olvasót.
c1-26-02.english: The quotation torn out of its context misleads the reader.
c1-26-02.canDo: I can describe a text with a participle before the noun (*a tényeket eltorzító*, *a kontextusból kiragadott*).

c1-26-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Refuting a Claim
c1-26-03.scenario: A news item says that all documents are public. You know that only a few are available.
c1-26-03.prompt: Tell Károly that the claim is wrong and what the facts are.
c1-26-03.target: A hír szerint minden irat nyilvános, ezzel szemben a valóságban csak néhány elérhető.
c1-26-03.english: According to the news all documents are public; in reality, however, only a few are available.
c1-26-03.canDo: I can refute a false claim with *ezzel szemben a valóságban* and *éppen ellenkezőleg*.

c1-26-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Duty of the Press
c1-26-04.scenario: Károly asks what a newspaper must do when it writes about a dispute.
c1-26-04.prompt: Tell Károly what the press must do.
c1-26-04.target: A sajtónak tárgyilagosan kell tájékoztatnia a közvéleményt.
c1-26-04.english: The press must inform the public objectively.
c1-26-04.canDo: I can say what the press or an editor must or must not do with *köteles*, *kell* and *nem … -hat/-het*.

c1-26-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Journalist's Conduct
c1-26-05.scenario: You have read an article about a reporter who published the facts despite threats. Károly asks what you think of his work.
c1-26-05.prompt: Tell Károly how the reporter worked.
c1-26-05.english: The reporter worked in a professionally irreproachable way.
c1-26-05.canDo: I can grade a person's conduct with a degree adverb (*szakmailag feddhetetlenül*, *erkölcsileg mélységesen aggályos*).

c1-26-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: An Unconfirmed News Item
c1-26-consolidation.scenario: Károly asks you what a good newspaper should do with a news item it cannot confirm.
c1-26-consolidation.prompt: Tell Károly how sure the news is and what the paper must do.
cues: Say how sure the news is
Say what the press must do
c1-26-consolidation.target: A hír feltehetőleg hamis, ezért a lapnak ellenőriznie kell a forrást.
c1-26-consolidation.english: The news is probably false, so the paper must check the source.
c1-26-consolidation.canDo: I can use the words for fact-checking, manipulation, rebuttal and press ethics.
